MS.summary: An Apr 18, 2026 byroot blog post discusses speeding up Ruby on Rails CI startup by optimizing Bootsnap’s load path caching. The author says Intercom’s monolith CI uses 1,350 parallel workers by default and reports that eliminating 1 second of setup time yields 1,350× more impact and “saves over 20 minutes of compute per build.” The post attributes Ruby boot slowdowns to $LOAD_PATH scanning during require: a “clean Ruby process” starts with ~8 load-path entries, and in the worst case Ruby may query the filesystem ~16 times; with many gems, load-path length grows and the cost is described as roughly O(N*M), where N=$LOAD_PATH.size and M=$LOADED_FEATURES.size. Bootsnap is described as eagerly scanning all $LOAD_PATH directories once to build a hash mapping requirable names to absolute paths (O(1) lookup) and using it to bypass Ruby’s linear load-path search during require. Cache invalidation is described via recording mtimes of scanned directories; if directories/files change, directory mtime updates are used for revalidation, and in CI (git checkouts) the cache often must be rebuilt, making scanning performance important. The post highlights an “N+1 syscalls” issue: Bootsnap’s scanner uses per-entry File.directory? checks (stat(2)), and the author says the Intercom monorepo load-path scan was “just shy of a second” 2. The proposed fix is to use a directory-walk API that avoids per-entry stat calls by using d_type from readdir(3); the author says implementing Dir.scan/prototypes by extending Dir methods to yield file type reduced recursive directory walking speed by about 2×. The work includes collaboration with Nobuyoshi Nakada ("nobu"), who proposed yielding File::Stat objects; the author says the approach could require Ruby 4.1 (waiting for approval from Matz). Named entities: Intercom, Ruby, Rails, Bootsnap, Aaron Patterson, Burke Libbey, Nobuyoshi Nakada (nobu), Matz, Shopify, Zeitwerk, GORUCO 2015.
MS.title: Optimizing Ruby Path Methods

AAPL.title: Apple’s China iPhone Surge Reshapes Growth And Margin Questions For Investors

AAPL.summary:
The US International Trade Commission (ITC) rejected Masimo’s bid to reinstate an import ban on Apple’s redesigned Apple Watch models. The ITC “terminate[d] the case” and referred to a March preliminary ruling that the redesigned watches do not infringe Masimo patents related to blood-oxygen monitoring. Apple said in a statement that “Masimo has waged a relentless legal campaign against Apple and nearly all of its claims have been rejected.”

Background facts: the dispute began in 2021 when Masimo filed for an import ban; the ITC previously found Apple violated Masimo patents, prompting a redesign of the blood-oxygen feature in certain models. After the redesign, Masimo sought a second import ban. The latest ITC decision leaves Masimo able to appeal to the US Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit.

Related litigation fact: in November, a federal jury ruled for Masimo in a separate patent infringement case and ordered Apple to pay $634 million.
AAPL.title: Apple avoids a second import ban for its redesigned smartwatches in latest court ruling

AAPL.summary:
- ITC: The U.S. International Trade Commission declined to review a prior ruling that cleared Apple Watch models redesigned by Apple of patent infringement claims. The decision was a blow to Masimo Corp. (NASDAQ: MASI), effectively ending Masimo’s attempt to reinstate a U.S. import ban tied to blood-oxygen sensing technology; Masimo alleges Apple copied the technology after hiring away its employees.

AAPL.title: Apple TV’s 10/10 Secret Sci-Fi Masterpiece Officially Returns This Summer

AAPL.summary: Jamf Threat Labs researchers described a ClickFix delivery workaround that bypasses Apple’s macOS Tahoe 26.4 Terminal paste warning. Instead of tricking users into pasting commands into Terminal, the attack uses a fake Apple-themed webpage (e.g., “Reclaim disk space on your Mac”) with an “Execute” button that launches an applescript:// URL scheme. Clicking “Execute” opens Script Editor with a pre-filled script; after the user clicks through Script Editor’s “unidentified developer” prompt, the script runs an obfuscated curl command to download and drop an infostealer/trojan payload such as Atomic Stealer. The post says this avoids the Tahoe 26.4 Terminal paste prompt because the command never touches Terminal.
AAPL.title: Security Bite: ClickFix malware authors already bypassing Apple’s new Terminal paste warning

AAPL.title: Apple @ Work: Free Apple device management is a baseline, not a finish line

AAPL.summary:
The U.S. International Trade Commission (ITC) declined to review a prior ruling that cleared Apple’s redesigned Apple Watch models from patent infringement in a dispute with Masimo (NASDAQ: MASI) involving blood-oxygen sensing technology. The ITC decision effectively ends Masimo’s attempt to reinstate a U.S. import ban on Apple Watch models. The dispute stems from Masimo’s claim that Apple copied its technology after hiring Masimo employees. Before the ITC review request, an ITC judge found Apple’s updated design does not violate the asserted patents.

Apple previously modified affected watches after a 2023 ITC ruling that blocked imports of certain models, including changing how blood-oxygen data is displayed by shifting key functions to paired devices such as the iPhone. Apple said in a statement that it can continue offering the “important health” feature and thanked the ITC; it also described Masimo’s efforts as a “relentless legal” campaign and said most claims have failed.

Masimo can appeal to the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit. The companies also have parallel litigation; Masimo obtained a $634 million verdict in a separate patent case in California that Apple plans to challenge.

Price data: Apple closed at $270.23 on Friday (+2.59%) and was $270.75 (+0.19%) in after-hours trading, per Benzinga Pro.
AAPL.title: Apple Scores Key Win As Trade Commission Rejects Masimo's Bid To Reinstate Apple Watch Import Ban

NVDA.title: Nebius Has Landed $46 Billion in AI Cloud Deals. Could This Stock 10X From Here?

NVDA.summary:
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang said he “doesn’t do one-on-one’s” with any of his 55 direct reports, while still holding regular catch-ups with his executive team. Huang described a goal of transparency without secret information to subsets of staff, and said limiting meetings helps the company move faster in the AI race; he added Nvidia was “designed for agility” with information flowing quickly to empower employees. Huang made these comments at the Stanford Institute for Economic Policy Research summit in 2024.

The article also cites other CEOs’ work-rule changes: Airbnb CEO Brian Chesky said he no longer emails (prefers texting/calling) and doesn’t take meetings before 10 a.m.; United Airlines CEO Scott Kirby said he takes about a 20-minute office nap; Southwest Airlines CEO Bob Jordan said his calendar is kept clear every Wednesday–Friday afternoon with no meetings in those hours; Twilio CEO Khozema Shipchandler said he typically holds 25-minute meetings in a 30-minute slot (and 50-minute meetings in an hour slot) and uses gaps for exercise.
NVDA.title: Jensen Huang bans one-on-one meetings, and Airbnb’s Brian Chesky doesn’t use email—meet the CEOs with unconventional work-life rules

NVDA.summary: Indeed CIO Anthony Moisant said the company will not implement an AI “token usage” leaderboard. Moisant told Business Insider that Indeed tracks token use “in the background” rather than tying it to incentives, citing “perverse incentive” risks when metrics like token counts are part of an incentive system. He said Indeed instead prioritizes outcomes such as faster product shipping and customer response, and specifically outcomes like “better matching” and “faster matching.” Moisant also said Indeed previously used “percentage of code written” as a productivity proxy for about three to four months (in the period when tools like Anthropic’s Claude Code and Cursor were gaining popularity) but stopped because it wasn’t reshaping productivity or changing outcomes. On AI costs, Moisant said Indeed’s AI bills are projected to be 4x higher than in 2025, mostly attributed to R&D usage, and that the board discussed balancing budget control with not slowing productivity. He said teams will be reviewed for “spiking” activity by looking for value tied to “time-to-value” (time from idea to shipping to customers). Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is cited saying a $500,000 engineer should use the equivalent of $250,000 in AI tokens.
NVDA.title: Top Indeed exec details why they'll never have a 'Tokenmaxxing'-esque leaderboard

NVDA.summary: CNBC (Apr 19, 2026) reported at two Silicon Valley events that scaling AI agents is still “rickety” and can become a “cost-sucker.” Kevin McGrath, CEO of AI startup Meibel, said a key problem is the belief that “everything needs to be processed by a large language model (LLM),” warning that “giving all of your tokens and all of your money to an AI Claw bot” could “waste millions and millions of tokens.” At the Generative AI and Agentic AI Summit in San Jose, Google software engineer Deep Shah said one major deployment issue is “inference cost,” and that poor monitoring of agent actions can “burn cash instead of saving it.” Ravi Bulusu, CEO of Synchtron, said the challenge is complexity across how companies organize data, choose platforms, build software, and manage workforces—calling interdependencies “chaotic.” In a Mountain View event, ThinkingAI (rebranded from ThinkingData) partnered with MiniMax, which went public in Hong Kong in January and is described as one of China’s “AI Tigers,” releasing models for free to the open-source community. ThinkingAI co-founder Chris Han said OpenClaw is “too complicated and too prone to security flaws for businesses,” stating it is suitable for personal use but “cannot reach the enterprise level” and that enterprise deployment requires solving memory, managing agents and teams, and communications. Han also said ThinkingAI can support models from OpenAI and Google, and declined to comment on national security concerns.
NVDA.title: SiIicon Valley's AI agent hiccups: Wasted tokens and 'chaotic' systems

NVDA.summary:
CNBC reports gamer backlash against Nvidia’s AI-driven priorities. Gamers say Nvidia is “left behind” as a memory shortage forces the company to prioritize data-center GPUs (Hopper, Blackwell) and the new Vera Rubin AI platform over GeForce gaming GPUs.

Key reported figures and named entities:
- Nvidia’s data center segment is 91.5% of revenue.
- Reported operating margins over the past three years: ~69% for Nvidia’s compute and networking segment vs ~40% for the consumer-forward graphics segment.
- 2026 may be the first year in three decades without a new GeForce generation, per the article; the current RTX 50 series was unveiled at CES in January 2025.
- Nvidia purchased Mellanox Technologies for $7 billion (2020), shifting focus toward AI GPUs.
- Analyst/estimate pricing contrasts: one Blackwell GPU costs up to ~$40,000 (analysts), and a full Vera Rubin system may cost up to ~$4 million (Futurum Group estimate). Nvidia’s RTX 50-series gaming GPUs are priced between $299 and $1,999.
- Memory constraints: industry reports suggest Nvidia plans to reduce production of its latest gaming GPUs by up to 40% due to general-purpose memory (DRAM) shortages.
- Gartner forecast in the article: PC prices up 17% in 2026 and PC shipments down 10.4%. The article also cites Gartner’s prediction that the entry-level consumer PC market could disappear by 2028.
- Storage/memory mix: Higher-performance GPUs like Blackwell and Rubin use HBM (High Bandwidth Memory); the article quotes Stacy Rasgon (Bernstein Research) saying it takes about 4x as many silicon wafers to make a gigabyte of HBM as traditional DRAM.

DLSS controversy:
- Nvidia unveiled DLSS 5 at GTC on March 16, 2026.
- Gamers object that DLSS 5 uses generative AI to change game visuals; examples cited include Resident Evil Requiem, Starfield, and Hogwarts Legacy.
- Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang said at GTC that AI will “revolutionize how computer graphics is done.”

Nvidia response:
- Nvidia told CNBC it is continuing to ship all GeForce GPUs it sees strong demand for and is working with suppliers to maximize memory availability.
NVDA.title: Nvidia's once-tight bond with gamers is cracking over AI, 'and that breaks my heart'

NVDA.summary: TipRanks (Apr 18, 2026) cites Oppenheimer analyst Rick Schafer, who rates Nvidia (NVDA) “Outperform” with a $265 price target and describes Nvidia as an “AI castle on a hill” with the best performance-per-watt for both training and inference. NVDA.title: Nvidia Stock Slaughters Rivals AMD & Intel as the as Blackwell Ultra Racks ‘Lead the Market by Two Generations’

NVDA.summary: AI coding startup Cursor (parent: Anysphere; founded by Michael Truell, Sualeh Asif, Arvid Lunnemark, Aman Sanger at MIT) is reported to be close to raising at least $2 billion at a $50 billion pre-money valuation. NVDA.title: AI Coding Startup Cursor Set For $2 Billion Funding Round, Nearly Doubling Valuation With Nvidia Backing: Report

NVDA.summary: A coder prankster, Riley Walz, built a side project called Lunches.fyi that ranks tech companies by cafeteria food quality using AI. Walz said he created it in about an hour by voice-dictating commands into OpenAI’s Codex, versus “20+ hours” previously. The site scrapes publicly available company menus and uses AI to categorize and score meals. Walz’s early results ranked Nvidia as a “surprise leader,” based on items such as “truffle mushroom pizza” and leafy greens. The experiment also triggered an example of an AI/data error: Replit CEO Amjad Masad publicly questioned Replit’s “low protein ranking.” Walz later said a bug caused missing nutrition data to be treated as 0 grams of protein for all Replit dishes; he fixed the issue after March 10, 2026.
NVDA.title: A coder used AI to rank which tech companies offer the best food at work. Check out the winners.

NVDA.summary:
Anthropic reported that CEO Dario Amodei met with “senior administration officials” at the White House on Friday to discuss cybersecurity, “America’s lead in the AI race,” and AI safety. Anthropic spokesperson Max Young said the meeting reflected Anthropic’s “ongoing commitment” to work with the US government. The article links the meeting to Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei’s earlier dispute with the Trump administration over two “red lines” after late-February Pentagon fallout: Anthropic would not agree to (1) using its technology for domestic mass surveillance or (2) deploying lethal fully autonomous weapons “with no human in the loop.” The earlier conflict included Anthropic being categorized as a “supply chain risk,” Anthropic filing a lawsuit against that designation, and a temporary injunction halting its ban.

The reported thaw is attributed to Anthropic’s new cybersecurity model, “Claude Mythos Preview” (announced with “major fanfare”). Anthropic says it can find security issues in “virtually every large web browser and operating system.” The model is described as Anthropic’s “most powerful yet” and is “currently only available for private access.” Anthropic says the model is intended to help identify high-stakes vulnerabilities in widely used internet infrastructure before “bad actors can exploit them.” The company says customer sign-ons include Apple, Nvidia, and JPMorgan Chase. The release also reportedly triggered emergency meetings between US bank leaders and Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell. The article says Anthropic is in “ongoing discussions” with US government officials about Claude Mythos Preview’s “offensive and defensive cyber capabilities.” Earlier, Dianne Penn (head of product management at Anthropic) told The Verge that Anthropic “briefed senior officials” about Mythos and what it can do, without naming who.

The article adds that Axios reported Amodei was scheduled for a meeting with White House chief of staff Susie Wiles, and that some parts of the US intelligence community and the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA, part of Homeland Security) are testing Mythos Preview, with other agencies interested. It also reports Anthropic recently hired Ballard Partners, a lobbying firm linked to Trump, and says this has fueled reports of a possible White House deal. The article suggests this could affect Pentagon views of Claude if government usage expands across agencies.
NVDA.title: Anthropic’s new cybersecurity model could get it back in the government’s good graces

WDAY.summary: ZDNET tested HP’s ZBook 8 G1i (14-inch) workstation (review dated April 18, 2026, by Kyle Kucharski). ZDNET reports the laptop runs “warm,” with more heat during file transfers or large installs, especially on the left side near the battery connection; heat was not described as exceeding “concerning levels.” Battery-life results cited: reaching about 20% around 2–3 p.m., with the remainder of the day sometimes “too close to zero” depending on workload. The included 140W power adapter is described as charging up to 50% in 30 minutes, while also increasing heat and causing fan activity. ZDNET’s stated score for the product is 3.5/5 (“Good”).
WDAY.title: After testing this HP laptop, I get why its 'boring' design is adored by business users

WDAY.summary: Karl-Anthony Towns (30), a New York Knicks player, describes his routine in a Business Insider “Power Hours” feature dated 2026-04-18. He wakes at 6:00 a.m. and drinks 16 ounces of water, followed by black coffee, MCT oil, and chicken bone broth. He practices starting at 7:00 a.m., and on game days (3 to 4 days per week during the season) focuses on hydration; he says players at the Knicks facility get hydration tested and are checked throughout the day. His strength/mobility work includes lunges (his stated favorite), chin-ups, and goblet squats; he previously had a meniscus tear and says it is the only surgery he has had. He strengthens feet with exercises like rolling out with a lacrosse or tennis ball and gripping/lowering a ball to work toe contraction. He takes “Advil” for swollen feet and mentions partnering with Advil to promote its Advil Exchange program. Meals typically include chicken with greens/vegetables, plus sweet potatoes, cauliflower rice, or quinoa (and sometimes white rice for more carbs during the season); snacks include unsalted almonds, a protein bar, and electrolytes. He says the team naps before each game for up to about two hours. Towns is a former Kentucky Wildcats player and started his NBA career with the Minnesota Timberwolves in 2015; he joined the Knicks in 2024. He cites his father as a basketball player/coach and says his high school team at St. Joseph High School in New Jersey won a state championship in 2014. His fiancé, Jordyn Woods, encourages him to vary meals (e.g., salmon or other fish).
WDAY.title: I'm Karl-Anthony Towns. Here's a day in my life on the New York Knicks, from a bone broth breakfast to 2-hour pre-game naps.

V.summary:
Twenty-nine people have died in U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) custody since October 2025, surpassing the prior fiscal-year record of 28 deaths set in 2004, according to government data cited by NPR.

The most recent case described is the April 16 ICE report on the April 12 death of 27-year-old Aled Damien Carbonell-Betancourt, a Cuban man held in ICE custody in Miami, Florida. ICE’s initial report listed the cause of death as “presumed suicide,” while the official cause is still under investigation. ICE said he entered the U.S. in 2024 without valid documents, later released under “parole,” and was arrested for resisting an officer with violence in 2025 before being transferred into ICE custody earlier in 2026.

Detentions have risen sharply during the Trump administration: NPR reports detentions are up more than 70% compared with the first year of the Biden administration, and there are about 60,000 people in immigration detention. DHS disputed claims of a death spike, saying (as of April 16) “death rates in custody under the Trump administration are 0.009% of the detained population,” and said detainees receive medical care; DHS also said detention is a “choice” and encouraged detainees to self-deport using the CBP Home App.

During a congressional hearing on April 16, acting ICE Director Todd Lyons said the fiscal-year deaths are high because ICE has the “highest amount in detention” since 2003 and said ICE spent “almost half a billion dollars” last fiscal year to ensure care. Lyons cited intake procedures including a complete physical within 14 days and being seen by a medical professional within 24 hours of admission; he also said he resigned hours after testifying.

NPR reports the deadliest facilities so far include Adelanto ICE Processing Center in Adelanto, California and Camp East Montana in El Paso, Texas, each with three detainee deaths. Causes listed in ICE initial reports include suicide, alcohol withdrawal, liver failure, and kidney failure; symptoms cited include shortness of breath. One Camp East Montana death was ruled a homicide by the El Paso County Medical Examiner’s Office.

That homicide case involves Geraldo Lunas Campos. DHS initially said he died after “medical distress” and claimed he became “disruptive while in line for medication” and was placed in segregation; later, the El Paso Medical Examiner ruled his death “asphyxia due to neck and torso compression.” The FBI is investigating. NPR says Campos had been convicted of multiple crimes, including petty larceny, unlawful possession of a weapon during a robbery, and sexual contact with a child under 11. His children are seeking eyewitness testimony for a wrongful-death lawsuit petition.
V.title: Deaths of migrants in ICE custody hit record high under Trump

META.summary: Paul Koeck describes a Discord bug involving the OG image proxy (images-ext-1.discordapp.net) that can reveal message view timing, read count, and approximate time-on-screen. Discord normally fetches and validates a link’s og:image server-side, then proxies the image; the proxy fetch populates a cache and should prevent sender-side tracking. Koeck’s proof-of-concept forces the proxy-cache to never fill by returning a real image for the initial validation request, then returning HTTP 500 Internal Server Error for subsequent proxy fetches. Discord’s client then retries the failed image six times with predictable delays: waits 2s, 3s, 4s, 5s, 6s between Requests 2–6 (roughly a ~20s default retry window; Koeck expands it past ~3 minutes by adding up to a 30s delay before each 500). Because each retry is an independent proxy fetch hitting the sender-controlled origin, the sender can log request bursts to infer (1) when a recipient opened the embed (first retry time), (2) how many recipients opened it (one burst per viewer, clustered by deterministic cadence), and (3) how long it stayed visible (how many of the six retries arrived before the client stops). Koeck also notes a Cloudflare caching interaction in front of Discord’s image proxy and uses a “warm-up” by posting in a throwaway channel and waiting 1–2 minutes to stabilize behavior. The article reports responsible disclosure: 2024-12-21 reported via HackerOne, 2025-01-03 triaged, 2025-01-15 validity confirmed and bounty paid with report resolved, 2025-02-10 public disclosure approved. It also includes techniques to hide the visible link/image (1x1 transparent PNG og:image and nearly invisible link text using Unicode italic lowercase rho U+1D75A as link label text like “[ 𝃚 ]( https://example.com/ )”).
META.title: Discord Read Receipts Exploit: When, How Often, How Long

Han also said ThinkingAI can support models from OpenAI and Google, and declined to comment on national security concerns.

It links the production update to a Texas expansion agreement in Brazoria County, describing power potential that could eventually reach “hundreds of megawatts.” The piece also states CLSK’s narrative projects $1.0 billion in revenue and $116… (final figure not shown in the provided text).

CLSK.summary:
Charles Edward (Capriole Investments) said every major publicly listed Bitcoin mining firm is planning to shift toward AI services. He cited an expected drop in BTC-related revenue from an average ~90% to ~30% over the next 2–3 years. He also said several miners plan to delay new ASIC purchases, running existing machines until end of life and redirecting future spending to AI infrastructure, and warned this could reduce network security if mining hardware investment falls.

Separately, TheEnergyMag reported public miners are selling BTC at the fastest pace since the late stage of the prior crypto bear market. The article states that public miner companies including MARA, Riot, Congo, CleanSpark (CLSK), and Bitdeer collectively sold more than 32,000 BTC in Q1 2026. It also notes Hashprice fell to about $33 per PH/s and cites the 2024 halving as reducing block rewards; it adds mining difficulty is far higher than in 2021. The article ties this miner selling and reduced buy-side demand to potential downward pressure on Bitcoin’s price, which was shown as trading around $76,990 on a 1D chart (BTCUSDT on TradingView).
CLSK.title: Expert Predicts What Will Happen To Bitcoin Price Amid The Miner Shift To AI

CLSK.summary:
Early 2026 conditions show heavy Bitcoin miner stress. The article says about 20% of the Bitcoin mining industry is operating at a loss. Hashprice (daily revenue per unit of computing power) has declined since July 2025 to about $33 per petahash per second per day, while many miners’ breakeven is around $35. 

Major publicly traded miners named—MARA, CleanSpark (CLSK), Riot, Cango, Core Scientific, and Bitdeer—collectively sold more than 32,000 BTC during the first three months of 2026, according to TheEnergyMag. The article adds this total exceeds what the same companies sold across all four quarters of 2025 and surpasses a prior quarterly record of roughly 20,000 BTC set in Q2 2022. 

CryptoQuant data cited states miners’ combined BTC holdings fell from more than 1.86 million BTC at end-2023 to about 1.8 million BTC (as of the article’s reference point). CoinShares’ Q1 2026 Bitcoin Mining Report warns of continued “capitulation” in the first half of 2026 for higher-cost operators unless Bitcoin price meaningfully recovers. 

It also notes Strategy (company/treasury operator; not CLSK) continued buying Bitcoin, with Michael Saylor indicating another purchase was in progress.
CLSK.title: Bitcoin Pressure Builds As Miners Dump 32K BTC In Just 3 Months

CLSK.summary: Bitcoin mining public companies sold a record 32,000 BTC in Q1 2026, exceeding their total sales for all of 2025 and surpassing Q2 2022 levels after the Terra (LUNA) collapse. Named major sellers: MARA Holdings, CleanSpark, Riot Platforms, Cango, Core Scientific, and Bitdeer. The article links the selling to record-low hashprice below $35 per PH/s per day; hashprice is cited around $33, with about 20% of the industry operating at a loss. It also cites rising mining difficulty, reduced block rewards after the 2024 halving, and high electricity costs. CryptoQuant data cited: public miners’ aggregate BTC reserves fell from 1.86 million BTC at end of 2023 to about 1.8 million BTC currently. CoinShares analysts warn further capitulation is expected in the first half of 2026 without a significant BTC price rise.
CLSK.title: Public Miners Sold Record 32,000 BTC in Q1 of 2026

CLSK.summary: Capriole Investments founder Charles Edwards said in an X post (Apr 17, 2026) that major listed Bitcoin miners are pivoting toward AI. Edwards’ snapshot claims all major public miners have “made statements to pivot to AI,” and that companies are targeting AI rather than BTC. Based on company disclosures, Edwards estimates revenue mix of ~86% from BTC and ~13% from AI; he projects BTC-related revenue could fall to ~30% within 2–3 years. Examples named: IREN Limited (formerly Iris Energy, Nasdaq-listed) positioning as an AI infrastructure provider; TeraWulf signaling AI-focused data center operations; Core Scientific increasing AI/high-performance computing revenue; Hut 8 and Bitdeer increasing AI/high-performance computing exposure. Edwards also cites stock performance over the prior year: IREN up 753%, TeraWulf up 722%, and Cipher Mining up 632% for higher AI exposure. He contrasts with slower movers/laggards: CleanSpark down 23% and MARA down 21% over two years. The article notes miners may delay upgrading Bitcoin mining hardware and instead direct new capital to AI data centers, which could slow expansion of network computing power (hashrate). Adam Back argued in a follow-up X post that a drop in hashrate is “good for miners,” potentially improving margins and reducing the need to sell Bitcoin to cover costs.
CLSK.title: Bitcoin Mining Shift to AI Threatens Blockchain Security Outlook: Capriole

CLSK.summary:
Public bitcoin miners sold a record 32,000 BTC in Q1 2026, exceeding full-year 2025 net sales and surpassing the roughly 20,000 BTC dumped during the Terra-Luna collapse in Q2 2022. Named miners reported as part of the selloff include MARA Holdings (MARA), CleanSpark (CLSK), Riot Platforms (RIOT), Cango (CANG), Core Scientific, and Bitdeer.

- Riot Platforms: sold 3,778 BTC in Q1 2026; proceeds nearly $289.5 million.

SPOT.summary:
Heineken, Coachella’s official beer sponsor for 23 consecutive years, debuted “The Clinker” at Heineken House during Coachella 2026 Weekend One (article dated April 18, 2026). “The Clinker” is a smart device that lights up when it comes into contact with another Clinker, signaling music compatibility. SPOT.summary:
MacRumors reports Apple is working on an overhaul of the iPad mini and iPad Air lineup. iPad mini 8 is expected to switch from LCD to OLED, using a single-stack LTPS panel (not the iPad Pro’s tandem OLED). The display is rumored to grow from 8.3 to 8.7 inches, with ProMotion possible. Chip details are split: code Apple published in August pointed to A19 Pro, while other evidence suggests the unreleased A20 Pro; N1 and C1X chips are also expected. Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman says Apple is also developing a more water-resistant iPad mini with an official IP rating, using a vibration-based speaker system that removes traditional speaker holes to reduce water ingress. The redesign is expected to make the chassis thinner and could raise pricing by about $100 to around $599. Launch is suggested for the second half of 2026 at the earliest (leaker “Instant Digital”).

For iPad Air, Apple is expected to update it in early 2027 with OLED as the headline change, again using a single-stack LTPS panel supplied by Samsung to keep costs down versus tandem OLED. After more than six years since the last redesign, it is expected to adopt a new design similar to the iPad mini and include the M5 chip. The next iPad Pro is expected in spring 2027 with an M6 chip and a vapor chamber cooling system similar to iPhone 17 Pro, but with no rumored design changes. The gap between Air and Pro is expected to narrow as Air adopts OLED and a thinner design. A more major upgrade may come with a long-rumored foldable iPad: Gurman expects an 18-inch display, with development hurdles around weight and display tech pushing it to no earlier than 2029 and a potential price up to $3,900 (up to about 3x the cost of the current 13-inch iPad Pro).
SPOT.title: The MacRumors Show: What's Next for the iPad

SPOT.summary:
Google Assistant is being phased out in favor of Gemini across multiple device platforms, with a mix of feature removals and scheduled deprecations. Key points cited: 
- Google confirmed that starting March 2026, Google Assistant will no longer be an option on Android devices in favor of Gemini (phones will not have a fallback Assistant).
- Google removed 18 Assistant features in early 2024, including voice control for rescheduling Google Calendar events and functions described as cookbook management.
- By peak transition in March 2026, another wave of “underutilized” Assistant features was stripped away.
- Specific Assist-related capabilities mentioned as removed or reduced include: intuitive multimedia controls (favor/share photos and query their locations by voice), Photo Frame and screen-setting voice commands, Interpreter Mode and the Family Bell (described as removed or reduced to manual routines).
- Driving Mode for Assistant was sunset, leaving a stripped-back Google Maps view.
- Assistant was shut down on LG webOS TVs.
- Assistant was pulled from Fitbit wearables including Sense 2 and Versa 4, with a stated requirement to move to Pixel Watch to keep wrist-based voice utility.
- On Chromebooks, Assistant lost functionality; Gemini became the default. The article references Chrome OS 134 starting the Gemini transition, and says Chromebook Plus users get more features with the switch.
- Android Auto has started rolling out Gemini more widely; Android Automotive is described as expected to be updated “in the coming months.”
Named entities and product lines referenced: Google Assistant, Gemini, Android, Google Home, Pixel, Chromebooks/Chrome OS 134/Chromebook Plus, Android Auto/Android Automotive, Google Maps, LG webOS TVs, Fitbit (Sense 2, Versa 4), Pixel Watch, Nest speakers and smart displays.
SPOT.title: What is happening with the Google Assistant? [Video]

SPOT.summary: Amazon is named in a Los Angeles Superior Court class action filed by plaintiff Bill Merewhuader alleging “software tethering” on older Fire TV Sticks. The suit targets the first- and second-generation Fire TV Stick devices released in 2014 and 2016, claiming Amazon limited “critical software updates” that allegedly made the devices “nearly inoperable,” including preventing delivery of “instant” content. The complaint alleges this “unfair” practice violated FTC expectations that buyers “generally expect that the devices they buy will work and keep working” and that Amazon deceived customers by omitting it could “brick” devices. The article notes the lawsuit was filed about two weeks before Amazon announced a new generation of Fire TV Sticks. It also references Amazon’s April 2026 plan to stop supporting Kindle models released before 2012 on May 20, 2026, which is estimated to affect about 2 million devices and create 624 tons of e-waste, while retaining existing libraries.
SPOT.title: Your Old Amazon Fire Stick Might Be Involved In This New Lawsuit - Here's Why

PINS.summary: Pinterest ran a “phone-free” installation at the 2026 Coachella Valley Music and Arts Festival at the Empire Polo Club in Indio, California. With visitors’ phones locked away in pouches, attendees designed custom accessories in a phone-free space and used an on-site makeup room rather than posting immediately. Pinterest said it is taking part for a third year and is using Coachella to reach Gen Z, stating 50% of its audience is Gen Z; Pinterest also said Gen Z is its “fastest growing demographic.” Pinterest’s vice president and global head of consumer marketing, Sarah Pollack, said Pinterest would “sacrifice” immediate coverage to support a long-term message. The article also reports Coachella tickets for 2026 sold out in four days last year, and estimated attendance of about 250,000 people across two weekends. The bill-headliners listed include Sabrina Carpenter, Justin Bieber, and Karol G; the event spans nine stages. Other brand activations mentioned: e.l.f. Beauty ran “e.l.f.scape to Balm Desert,” which drew a “six-figure audience,” with lip glosses, slushies, and makeup touch-ups; Absolut vodka set up “Absolut Heat Haus,” described as a nightclub-style area with bars and a DJ, where Paris Hilton was the DJ last year.
PINS.title: Branded pop-up events take center stage at Coachella

PINS.summary:
Rolling Stone reports that Coachella (held two weekends in April at Empire Polo Club in Indio, California) has become a major creator-marketing revenue driver, with an estimated 375,000 visitors attending in 2026. The article states that Coachella began in 1999 and reached profitability in the late 2000s; beginning in 2011, festival executives added brand integrations (pop-ups, sponsored parties, and activations). 

Concrete creator pay/examples cited: a TikTok creator “Justine O.” (300,000+ followers) attended three times—2024 with VIP tickets plus covered transportation/hotel/food (no cash), and 2025 with the same perks plus $25,000. Emmy Hartman (26, 2.3 million TikTok followers) says a brand deal was “locked in” for Coachella but was canceled the week of the festival; she did not name the brand. Another creator, Micky Gordon (“Mickychella,” 1.1 million TikTok followers), describes a Poppi-paid brand trip: Gordon and “10 plus ones” stayed at an AirBnB described as the “Mick Mansion.” 

Named brands/companies and controversies mentioned: Starbucks is referenced as having a pop-up that drew backlash tied to alleged anti-union/anti-Palestinian actions; a popular skit from Benton McClintock jokes about attending Coachella with Lockheed Martin. The article also includes Sarah Pollack, VP global head of consumer marketing at Pinterest, saying brands measure success via impressions and that influencer cohorts can generate more social impressions than a month of consistent brand-team marketing.

The article also says some brands are shifting toward one or two big-name creators rather than multiple creators, leading to reports that creators were uninvited by brands before the first weekend as brands seek “the most bang for their buck.”
PINS.title: It Started as a Festival. Now Coachella Means Cash for Creators

PINS.summary:

Despite these points, the piece reports a TipRanks analyst rating of “Buy” for PINS.
PINS.title: Pinterest (PINS) Has Been Punished for Three Quarters. What’s Changed This Time?

PINS.title: 'This is not fun and games…’: OpenAI exec says AI 'doomers' are holding back the ‘incredible economic opportunities’ the tech can provide for ‘families and for society writ large’

MRK.summary: Canada has approved new RSV prevention tools: vaccines for older adults and pregnant people, and a long-acting monoclonal antibody (nirsevimab) intended to protect infants through their first RSV season with a single dose. The National Advisory Committee on Immunization (NACI) recommends universal infant RSV immunization but allows provinces to phase implementation based on “supply and cost,” while provinces decide what is publicly funded and for whom. The article says access is therefore a “patchwork” across provinces: some provinces expand infant coverage, while others limit publicly funded access to infants considered high risk; adult and maternal RSV programs also vary by eligibility, delivery, and funding. The piece attributes differences partly to high costs of RSV therapies, differing disease burden, and added challenges vaccinating northern/remote communities. It also highlights governance and transparency gaps: provincial budgets and priorities create no single body accountable for national equity; vaccine procurement pricing and contract terms “are not routinely disclosed,” and negotiations with manufacturers are often confidential. It notes that during COVID-19, federal vaccine contract details were released only after parliamentary pressure and with key information heavily redacted. The article frames RSV as an early post-pandemic test of Canada’s immunization system and argues that without clearer coordination, transparency, and shared expectations, new technologies may reinforce geographic variation in access.
MRK.title: Postal codes shouldn’t determine protection: What RSV reveals about vaccine equity in Canada

MRK.summary:
Merck (MRK) is compared with Novartis (NVS) as a “better pharma dividend stock.” Merck is cited as having a “forward” dividend yield around 2.9% and having increased dividends by 93.8% over the past decade. Merck’s current market data in the article: $119.01 share price (+3.08% / +$3.55), $294B market cap, 52-week range $73.31–$125.14, gross margin 74.21%, and dividend yield 2.79%. The article states Merck’s HPV vaccine sales (Gardasil and Gardasil 9) have declined due to issues in Asia, and that Keytruda will lose patent exclusivity within the next two years. It says Merck received approval for a new subcutaneous Keytruda version that is faster/easier to administer with similar efficacy, and that Keytruda is “the world’s best-selling cancer drug.” It also cites Winrevair (pulmonary arterial hypertension) as exceeding $1 billion in annual sales in 2025, and says Merck’s pneumonia vaccine Capvaxive is posting strong sales growth. For the pipeline, it highlights CD388, an investigational long-acting antiviral for influenza vaccination. 

Novartis is described as having lost U.S. patent exclusivity last year for Entresto (chronic heart failure) and as projecting “decent sales growth in 2026.” The article cites Novartis gross margin 75.02% and dividend yield 3.12%, with a forward yield of about 3.1% and dividend increases of 84.2% over the past decade (and paying dividends every year since 1996). It states 15 Novartis medicines generated over $1 billion in annual sales last year (with most showing year-over-year revenue growth). NVAX.summary: Sanofi reported head-to-head, double-blind, randomized Phase 4 results from the COMPARE study presented at the ESCMID Global Congress in Munich, Germany. The study enrolled 1,000 adults in the US and compared protein-based, adjuvanted Nuvaxovid (NVX-CoV2705; Sanofi; originally licensed by Novavax) versus mNEXSPIKE (mRNA-1283; Moderna). Nuvaxovid showed lower systemic reactogenicity across all pre-specified endpoints. The primary endpoint (probability of at least one systemic reaction within 7 days) occurred in 83.6% of Nuvaxovid recipients vs 91.6% of mNEXSPIKE recipients (risk difference 8.0%; 95% CI 4.0%–12%; p<0.001). Moderate-to-severe systemic symptoms (Grade 2–3) were reported by 43.1% with Nuvaxovid vs 61.3% with mNEXSPIKE (risk difference 18%; 95% CI 12%–24%; p<0.001). Moderate-to-severe local symptoms occurred in 38.7% vs 58.7% (risk difference 20%; 95% CI 14%–26%; p<0.001). Severe systemic symptoms that prevented normal daily activities were “more than 50% less frequent” with Nuvaxovid, affecting fewer than 1 in 10 recipients vs about 1 in 5 with mNEXSPIKE. Sanofi said participants receiving Nuvaxovid were nearly twice as likely to say they would “definitely choose the same vaccine type again” for the next year. Sanofi also stated Nuvaxovid caused less disruption to work, school, recreational activities, and caretaking over the 7-day period.
NVAX.title: Press Release: ESCMID: Sanofi's Nuvaxovid COVID-19 vaccine showed better tolerability than mNEXSPIKE in head-to-head study
